summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (a privacy-first encrypted cloud storage system) — porting the node/v3 model to the Rust desktop stack (FUSE/WinFsp), making clients grant-root-aware, and mirroring the TS Phase 68.2 SDK-owned read chain — via the GSD plan-phase then execute-phase workflows, with the user authorizing auto-advance from planning into unattended parallel execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (grew from 14 to 18 plans across three re-scopes) and 13/18 plans are merged and green, delivering the full crates/core + crates/sdk node/v3 foundation (codec, AAD seal, gated read-chain, resumable rotation engine, emit API, write-owner materialization). The final FUSE consumer cutover (69-09) proved to be a >1000-site, ~12k-LOC atomic rewrite; it is being landed via a sliced multi-session grind on a dedicated branch (4 of 5 slices done, errors down from 120 to 35) gated on a live sdk-e2e/desktop-e2e run rather than compile-green before merging.

repo: GSD commit helper reports 'commit_failed' as a false negative even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never retry blindly.

Worktree executors sometimes mis-report `expected_base` in their metadata (their own last docs commit instead of the true fork point) — verify with `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.
`cargo fmt` run from a crate root can reformat unrelated files across the whole crate; executors must diff-scope-check and revert out-of-scope reformats before committing.
Fresh worktrees lack `node_modules`, so the husky/lint-staged pre-commit hook fails on the first commit; either run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` or use `--no-verify` for pure-Rust changes.

The Unix FUSE mount is a read-write vault owner (it signs IPNS records and seals new children), unlike the web's read-only Phase 68.2 mirror — this invalidated the original phase 69 scope multiple times.

`ResolvedChild` (read-only listing) unseals then immediately zeroizes child keys (D-09) — it cannot be reused to materialize a writable tree; a separate `ResolvedOwnedChild`/`list_folder_owned` API was needed.

The legacy `JournalOp` wire format is hex-string, ECIES-under-user-public-key — structurally incompatible with node/v3's symmetric parent-key sealing; required its own reshape plan (69-18) rather than a simple field repoint.
`ApiNodeFetcher` is a lifetime-bound borrow adapter with no `::new` constructor — it must be constructed inline at each call site, not stored as a struct field (would be self-referential).
`CipherBoxFS` has only 3 real struct-literal construction sites (test_support.rs, desktop mod.rs, desktop windows/mod.rs), not the 6 originally assumed.
`NodeContent.file_iv` must be hex-encoded to match `content_ops.rs`'s `hex::decode` path.

D-07 dual-keying: read plane keyed by ipnsName (`SealedChildRef`), write plane keyed by childId UUID (`WriteChildRef`); canonical child id is `uuid_from_ino(child_ino)`, used consistently in both planes.
SC#6 requires a single shared gated-resolve entrypoint — no raw `resolve_published_node`/`resolve_ipns_verified` calls may exist in `crates/fuse`.

code.finding: Original research cited a `JournalOp::MkdirPublish.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` cross-crate weld here — this field does not actually exist; the real `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` lives in the fuse-side `MkdirJournalResult` (journal_helpers.rs:97), not in the cross-crate JournalOp.
`resolve_child` unseals the child read-key and immediately zeroizes it — never touches the write-body — making the read-only listing path unusable for write-owner materialization.

`InodeKind::{Root,Folder,File}` stores `ipns_private_key`/`folder_key`/`file_key` for signing IPNS records — a full read-write owner state requiring the entire enum reshape, not just a read-path swap.

`list_folder_owned` (added in 69-17) is the gated write-plane tree-materialization entrypoint returning `ResolvedOwnedChild{read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key}` via the same SC#6 gate as `list_folder`.
`seal_node` originally sealed only the read-body; `seal_published_node` (added in 69-15) seals both read and write bodies so `PublishedNode.write_sealed` is actually populated.

workflow: Canary pattern: dispatch the first plan in a wave synchronously and validate the full executor→worktree→merge→cargo pipeline before fanning out the rest in parallel.

Session/usage-limit deaths (API errors, stalled mid-stream) look identical to architectural blockers in task notifications — always check whether the worktree has zero edits (usage death, safe to retry after reset) versus a reasoned halt with evidence (architectural, needs re-scope) before reacting.

For large atomic changes that can't reach a compiling sub-unit, split into sequential 'slices' landed as commits on one shared branch, with a committed runbook capturing the frozen target shape and each slice's carry-forward facts — this lets the grind survive session interruption without losing coherence.
Before accepting a sub-agent's architectural-blocker claim, independently verify its grep/line-count evidence against the live tree rather than relaying it uncritically.

When an orchestrator has already authored the design brief and reviewed newly-planned files in full, it can skip a separate plan-checker agent to conserve a usage round — but only when confidence is genuinely high.
For genuinely high-risk atomic migrations (compiles RED mid-flip, vault-data correctness at stake), gate the merge on a real end-to-end test run instead of `cargo check --workspace` alone.
ScheduleWakeup + a durable scratchpad handoff file lets a long-running plan/execute session pause and resume cleanly at a specific time without losing state.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run with an API error, leaving 13/14 plans on disk and requiring filesystem-fallback recovery.
GSD's commit helper produces false-negative 'commit_failed' reports on essentially every commit, requiring manual git log verification each time.
Executors intermittently mis-report their worktree's `expected_base`, risking a bad merge if not independently verified.
Two separate opus executor sessions died from account/session usage limits mid-task (once during exploration, once mid-flip), interrupting the atomic 69-09 cutover.

The FUSE cutover (69-09) triggered three successive architectural re-scopes as deeper missing infrastructure was discovered each time (missing write-plane emit API → missing read-write owner materialization API → stale JournalOp weld assumption plus the real >1000-site InodeKind rewrite), each requiring a new AskUserQuestion decision point.
Working directory drifted mid-session, causing a commit command to fail until absolute paths were used.
A scratchpad handoff file was initially written to a mistyped, doubled path and had to be relocated.
open_items: 69-09 atomic FUSE cutover: Slice 5 (gated file-node fetch via new `fetch_node_gated`, remaining read_ops/dir_ops/poll/fs.rs glue, desktop wiring, SC#6 CI gate) still to be executed to reach cargo-green.
Combined 69-18+69-09 merge is pending, gated on a live local sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e (docker + TEE) run rather than just compile-green.
69-10 (delete legacy crates/core types, D-04) and 69-13 (grant-gated delete/rename + SC#2 + D-07) still queued after 69-09 lands.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows + TEST-03, `autonomous:false`) deferred as a hand-off to the user's Windows machine.
File versioning (`NodeContent.versions`) restore path noted as a regression to verify at E2E — not reconstructed at upload time.
Replay does not unpin the old parent CID after re-publish — orphaned IPFS pins accumulate (flagged as GC-able, non-blocking).
